page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a base clock speed of 2.4 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 937 GB NVMe SSD. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core and single-threaded performance. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and a text processing score of 2785.0. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are also strong, with gzip compression reaching 34.34 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.1 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling present a relative tradeoff, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth also shows a divergence, maintaining average speeds for small cached blocks but dropping to the bottom 25% for large uncached blocks.

Given its hardware profile, the i7i.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high local storage performance and substantial memory capacity per core without needing massive multi-core compute scaling. The combination of 32.0 GB of DDR5 RAM and a 937 GB NVMe SSD makes it well-suited for database operations, caching layers, and localized data processing. This is supported by average-tier Passmark database operations and Redis SET performance of 6.18 million operations per second. It is less suited for highly parallelized multi-threaded compilation or heavy multi-core compute tasks.

Qualitatively, the instance provides a balanced resource density for memory-intensive and storage-reliant workloads. It is highly suited for database operations, local caching, and single-threaded data processing tasks, while being less optimal for highly parallelized multi-core computing.
